subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle, Telegram first

question: Should OpenClaw permanently publish this narrowed core ingress-drain and turn-adoption lifecycle through the plugin runtime and channel-outbound SDK, or keep the first implementation internal while the contract matures?
rationale: The generic core ownership aligns with repository architecture and the patch is well-proven, but adding callable plugin API and compatibility mirrors creates a long-lived external contract that automation cannot authorize from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the narrowed public seam
options.body: Accept the documented factory, lifecycle binding, constants, types, and process helper as the permanent plugin contract once exact-head gates finish.

options.title: Keep the first version internal
options.body: Land the core and Telegram architecture without public plugin exposure, then publish a smaller API after another bundled channel validates the abstraction.

options.title: Split architecture from migration
options.body: Pause this branch and land the shared lifecycle/drain foundation separately from the Telegram transport migration to reduce one-merge blast radius.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrowed public seam
recommendation.body: Accept the documented factory, lifecycle binding, constants, types, and process helper as the permanent plugin contract once exact-head gates finish.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged SDK-surface narrowing and shared channel-runtime refactors make this the strongest available history-based owner for the permanent API boundary.
